RUNZERO_SEARCH.description: Server-side runZero query forwarded verbatim as a ?search=<value> query-string parameter to GET /api/v1.0/org/assets and GET /api/v1.0/org/services. Optional; empty / blank walks the entire organization's inventory (the dispatcher's token scope still applies). runZero's search syntax is rich: predicates like 'type:server os:linux', 'site:HQ alive:true', 'tag:pci', 'last_seen:<1d', and free-text terms are all supported and shared across both endpoints. Useful for sharding inventory pulls across multiple discovery profiles so each dispatcher agent only walks one slice of the organization per run. Whitespace is trimmed.

RUNZERO_LIMIT.description: Per-page record cap forwarded as a ?limit=<value> query-string parameter to both /assets and /services. Optional; defaults to 1000 (runZero's documented default). Accepts integer / numeric-string; floats are floored. Clamped to [1, 5000] in-executor — values above 5000 are silently clamped because that's runZero's documented hard cap per page. Pagination is offset-based on both surfaces (offset += limit per request) so a smaller limit means more requests; tune for the size of the target organization.

name: runzero
title: runZero
description: runZero asset-inventory importer. Pulls discovered assets and observed services from a runZero (runzero.com, formerly Rumble Network Discovery) console via the runZero v1.0 REST API and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Each runZero asset becomes one Faraday host (the asset's first non-loopback IP from addresses with addresses_extra as a fallback maps onto host.ip — loopback / 0.0.0.0 / ::1 are explicitly skipped and the executor falls back to a 0.0.0.0 sentinel when nothing usable is found; the names projection lands on host.hostnames; the first macs entry lands on host.mac; and the os / os_vendor / os_product / os_version / hw / hw_vendor chain joins onto host.os). Each runZero service from /api/v1.0/org/services becomes one synthetic Faraday host keyed on the service's address field (services ARE IP-keyed in runZero) so the workspace still surfaces the per-port discovery alongside the asset inventory; the service port / protocol / service_product projection lands on host.hostnames and the per-service banner / summary fields are embedded in the vulnerability description. The asset itself becomes one Faraday vulnerability with the [ASSET-INVENTORY] engine prefix so the data lands in the Faraday workspace alongside the other CMDB-class feeds (Axonius, Device42, Fleet, Armis, Jamf Pro, Jira Insight). Endpoints used: GET /api/v1.0/org/assets?search=...&limit=N&offset=M (paginated asset inventory; returns a bare JSON list of asset records with each record carrying id, organization_id, site_id, site_name, addresses, addresses_extra, mac_vendors, macs, names, os, os_vendor, os_product, os_version, hw, hw_vendor, hw_product, hw_version, type, tags, last_seen, first_seen, service_count, service_ports_products, service_ports_protocols, attributes), and GET /api/v1.0/org/services?search=...&limit=N&offset=M (the per-port service inventory; returns a bare JSON list of service records with each record carrying id, asset_id, address, port, protocol, transport, service_protocol, service_summary, service_vendor, service_product, service_version, last_seen, first_seen, attributes). RUNZERO_SEARCH is forwarded verbatim to both surfaces so a single query scopes both walks consistently (runZero shares the search syntax across the two endpoints). Walked page-by-page (offset-based) until len(records) < limit or RUNZERO_PAGES (env-only override, default 5, clamped to [1, 50]) is reached. RUNZERO_LIMIT controls the per-page cap (default 1000, clamped to [1, 5000]). Severity is always info because runZero hits are inventory entries, not vulnerability findings — operators correlate against the EDR / EASM / vuln-scanner agents' findings via the RunZero-Id / RunZero-Site / RunZero-Type / RunZero-LastSeen / RunZero-OSVersion / RunZero-Tags / RunZero-ServiceCount refs on asset hits, and the RunZero-ServiceId / RunZero-AssetId / RunZero-Port / RunZero-Protocol / RunZero-Product / RunZero-LastSeen refs on service hits. Auth: runZero uses long-lived organization API keys generated via the runZero console under Account -> API Keys (pick an Organization-scoped key, NOT an Account-scoped one). The dispatcher carries the token on every request as the standard Authorization: Bearer <RUNZERO_TOKEN> header. RUNZERO_HOST defaults to console.runzero.com (the SaaS console); on-prem / self-hosted appliances are common so we also tolerate runzero.mycorp.local and add https:// automatically when the operator pasted in a bare FQDN. Tags: [runzero, asset-inventory, asset|service].
